newsitem.title: CHINA: HSBC Holdings eases on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: HSBC Holdings eases on profit-taking.

text.p: Shares of HSBC Holdings Plc were hit by profit-taking on Friday morning after repeatedly setting records this week, brokers said.
The shares slipped HK$11.00 to HK$268.00 on very heavy turnover of HK$751.43 million.
On Thursday, HSBC shares soared HK$15.00 to close at an all-time high of HK$279.00. HSBC fell HK$5.50 to HK$273.50 in London overnight. "It is just profit-taking," said a broker at a British house.
HSBC has been pushed to higher levels by index funds seeking the appropriate weighting in U.K.-listed banks as well as institutional investors and hedge funds in Hong Kong.
It is also a favourite of regional traders seeking a stable, liquid investment in a stable currency, brokers said.
HSBC is due to announce its results for the first six months of 1997 on August 4.
Expectations for the banking giant's earnings growth fall within a wide range of six to 20 percent, brokers said.
